slides.headline: Every distributed system has to give up *something*.
subtitle: The CAP theorem: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance.
Here is what each one means.
slides.narration: Every distributed system has to give up something. The CAP theorem is about three things: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance. Here is what each one means.

slides.heading: Consistency: every read is *current*
body: Every node returns the same, most recent value.
Deposit 500 on node A, then check node B: you see 500, never an old 400.
slides.narration: Consistency means every read is current. Every node returns the same, most recent value. If you deposit 500 on node A and then check node B, you see 500, never an old 400. Users never see conflicting data.

slides.heading: Availability: every request gets *an answer*
body: Every request sent to a working node gets a response.
The answer may be a little stale, but it always comes back.
A system that times out or refuses requests is not available.
slides.narration: Availability means every request gets an answer. Every request sent to a working node gets a response. The answer may be a little stale, but it always comes back. A system that times out or refuses requests is not available.

slides.heading: Partition tolerance: the *network splits*
body: Machines talk over network links, and links fail.
A partition cuts the cluster into groups that cannot reach each other.
The system must keep running through it, so plan for it.
slides.narration: Partition tolerance means the system keeps working when the network splits. Machines talk over network links, and links fail. A partition cuts the cluster into groups that cannot reach each other. So the system must keep running through it, and you have to plan for it.

slides.heading: During a partition, you *choose*
body: Refuse some requests to keep the data consistent: that is CP.
Or answer every request, even with stale data: that is AP.
The theorem forces this choice, so you cannot skip it.
slides.narration: During a partition, you have to choose. You can refuse some requests to keep the data consistent, which is a CP system. Or you can answer every request, even with stale data, which is an AP system. The theorem forces this choice, so you cannot skip it.

slides.headline: Ask what it does during a partition.
slides.cta: Follow vivektraces for the next one.
slides.narration: So when a database is called fast or safe, ask what it does during a partition. Follow vivektraces for the next one.
